Article 17
Protection of women and children is a shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Parents, Guardians and/or Family;
c. Community; and
d. Business sector/private sector.

Article 12
Other violence as referred to in Article letter constitutes threat of violence and coercion.
(1) Threat of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes every unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause (2) fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own (3) will.

Article 11
Exploitation as referred to in Article letter includes: acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
a.
acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced work or
b.
services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution activities or sexual abuse.

Article 41
In order to achieve the objectives of protection of women and children as referred to in Article 4, Regional Governments may cooperate with other parties in accordance with (1) the provisions of laws and regulations.
The cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: (2)
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses.
The cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (3) (2) shall be set forth in the form of a Joint Agreement and/or Cooperation Agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 10
Neglect as referred to in Article letter includes: a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women and children within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women; and/or
d. acts that result in economic dependency by means of restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of such person.

2.3.rationale: In the Indonesian text, Pasal 41 ayat (2) huruf a indeed says cooperation includes "pertukaran data dan informasi" (exchange of data and information). However, the indicator is about having a data collection / information system (a mechanism/system for collecting, managing, and using data), not merely mentioning data exchange as one possible cooperation activity. The retrieved passage does not establish any system (e.g., database, case registry, reporting system, data management unit, routine data collection). The judge over-interpreted “exchange of data and information” as implying an information system, leading to a false positive.

2.6.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences reference minimum service standards and accompaniment that includes monitoring victims’ interests during legal processes, but they do not establish monitoring and evaluation of overall policy implementation and service delivery (e.g., M&E framework, reporting, evaluation responsibilities).

2.6.rationale: The Indonesian text contains an explicit monitoring element in Pasal 28 huruf c: "memantau kepentingan dan hak-hak korban" (to monitor the interests and rights of victims) during police/prosecutor/court examination processes. This is a form of monitoring within service delivery (victim accompaniment), even if it is not a full policy-wide M&E framework. Because the indicator is “Monitoring and evaluation” (not necessarily requiring a full M&E system), the document does include monitoring language, and the relevant sentence was present in the retrieved candidates. The judge’s ‘No’ was based on a narrower interpretation (overall policy M&E only), so the golden “Yes” appears defensible and likely correct.

3.8.evaluator_rationale: Although the policy mentions that social rehabilitation is implemented by regional apparatus including the field of 'mental and spiritual', the provided sentences do not explicitly state that victims receive religious/spiritual counseling, guidance, or faith-based mentoring as a service.

3.8.rationale: The Indonesian text (Pasal 32 ayat (4) huruf e) states social rehabilitation is implemented by regional apparatus in the field of "mental dan spiritual". While it does not explicitly say “religious counseling” (konseling keagamaan) by name, “mental and spiritual” support in Indonesian policy drafting commonly covers spiritual/religious guidance, and the same article also lists "bimbingan dan konseling" as part of rehabilitation (Pasal 32 ayat (2) huruf a). Given the indicator is religious/spiritual counselling, the combination of (i) counseling/guidance being provided and (ii) implementation by the ‘mental and spiritual’ sector supports a ‘Yes’. The judge required more explicit wording than the regulation provides; thus the golden label likely reflects the intended meaning of the text.

6.3.rationale: The Indonesian text Pasal 13 lists women’s rights, including: "memperoleh pekerjaan yang layak" (huruf d) and "mendapatkan perlindungan khusus dalam pelaksanaan pekerjaan atau profesinya... berkenaan dengan fungsi reproduksi perempuan" (huruf g). This is explicitly about protections related to women in work/profession (i.e., women workers). The retrieved English passage accurately reflects this. If the indicator “Women workers” is satisfied by explicit worker-related protections/rights for women, then the correct label should be Yes, meaning the golden ‘No’ appears incorrect.
